advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm esbuild writes `dist/roundtrip.mjs` atomically; if not, gate the unlocked fast-path `_satisfied` (tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:151) so a completeness signal (e.g. a sentinel written after build, or a done-marker) is required before returning without the lock.
evidence: Shared resource: `dist/roundtrip.mjs` bundle in `tests/e2e/js`, written by `npm run build` — `_run_step("npm run build", [npm, "run", "build"], js_dir, build_timeout)` (tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:173)

Second executor: pytest-xdist worker processes, `-n 4 --dist worksteal` — cited in conftest.py:63 ('under -n 4 --dist worksteal every worker runs the fixture') and exercised by tests/e2e/test_toolchain_provisioning.py `test_two_concurrent_workers_do_not_overlap_their_install_steps` which spawns 2 subprocess.Popen provisioners
Unlocked READ: `if _satisfied(js_dir, with_browser=with_browser): return` (tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:151-152), executing BEFORE `with _install_lock(js_dir):` at line 164
`_satisfied` tests only existence, not completeness: `... and (js_dir / BUNDLE_RELPATH).is_file()` (tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:124)

Sibling accessor with the guard: the SAME `_satisfied` re-check is performed UNDER the lock at tests/e2e/_toolchain.py:168 (`with _install_lock` opened at line 164); the fast-path copy at 151 is the unlocked twin
WRITE: esbuild bundle emission inside `npm run build` (line 173), running while the writer holds LOCK_EX (line 164) — a peer's line-151 read is not serialized against it

Harm (conditional): a reader observes a truncated/partial `roundtrip.mjs` and the fixture runs it, producing a spurious harness failure/corrupted round-trip result rather than a skip; contingent on esbuild NOT writing the bundle atomically (temp+rename), which Pass-2 should confirm
advisory.finding: `provision_toolchain`'s unlocked fast-path `_satisfied()` check (before the flock) treats the harness bundle as ready on mere existence (`bundle.is_file()`), so a worker can return early and run `node dist/roundtrip.mjs` while another lock-holding worker is still writing that bundle via `npm run build` — a partial-file read of a shared artifact the lock was meant to protect.
scenarios: Cold `tests/e2e/js` under `pytest tests/e2e -n 4 --dist worksteal`: worker A holds the lock building the bundle; worker B (not yet in the lock) hits the line-151 fast path just as the bundle file appears and skips locking, then executes a half-written bundle.

advisory.finding: The CI `make e2e-deps` target runs `npm ci` (full tree, browser stack included) but no workflow step provisions the actual browser binaries (`npx playwright install chromium`); combined with `browser_runner` self-skipping when 'Chromium unavailable', browser-tier e2e tests silently skip in CI even after the toolchain is provisioned.
scenarios: CI runs the e2e browser tier expecting coverage but every browser test skips because the Chromium download was never fetched

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the npm cache restore-keys fallback cannot yield non-reproducible installs on the non-lockfile fallback path.
evidence: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:475-476: `restore-keys:` keyed only on `${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version }}-` (no lockfile hash)
_toolchain.py: `verb = "ci" if (js_dir / "package-lock.json").is_file() else "install"` — install path is non-lockfile-exact
advisory.finding: The npm cache restore-keys fallback (`${{ runner.os }}-npm-${{ steps.e2e-node.outputs.node-version }}-`) will restore a `~/.npm` populated under a different lockfile; this is only drift-safe because `make e2e-deps` uses `npm ci`, but the in-fixture fallback path may use `npm install` (when no lockfile), which could resolve differently against a warm-but-stale cache.
scenarios: A future e2e tree without a committed lockfile hitting a warm ~/.npm restored from a different dependency set

evidence: conftest.py:79-82: `try: provision_toolchain(...) except ToolchainProvisioningError as exc: _PROVISION_ERROR = str(exc)`
_toolchain.py:73: `js_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` and 74-75 open/flock — these can raise OSError, which is NOT a ToolchainProvisioningError.
The fixture fallbacks (conftest.py:99-102, 141-144) have the same narrow except, so a non-ToolchainProvisioningError there aborts the test instead of skipping.
dropped.finding: `pytest_collection_modifyitems` only catches `ToolchainProvisioningError`. Any other exception raised during provisioning (e.g. an OSError from `js_dir.mkdir` in `_install_lock`, a permission error on the lock file, or a fcntl error) propagates out of the collection hook and aborts collection for the entire e2e tier, rather than degrading to a skip as the tier's opt-in/self-skipping contract promises.

dropped.finding: When a session reaches the bpmn_harness fixture fallback without the collection hook or `make e2e-deps` having provisioned (e.g. the hook returned early because Node was absent at collection but present later, or an odd invocation path), and a browser test is also selected, bpmn_harness provisions with with_browser=False and browser_runner then re-runs a full `npm ci`, double-installing node_modules. This is a redundant cost, not a correctness bug, but it undercuts the 'install once' intent for that fallback path.
